core_ideas.idea: Prompt engineering is the control layer - from natural language to structured JSON and chat commands
core_ideas.why: It lets beginners create and edit video without timelines, and get precise cinematic control in tools like Veo 3 just by typing
core_ideas.trade_off: Natural prompts are easy but vague; JSON and advanced chat prompts are powerful but take time to learn and can still need manual fixing

core_ideas.idea: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) gives LLMs fresh knowledge without retraining
core_ideas.why: Instead of fine-tuning, you index your own docs, turn them into vector embeddings with tools like ChromaDB, and retrieve answers - as shown in the Obelisk MkDocs chatbot
core_ideas.trade_off: Cheaper and faster than training, but quality depends on chunking, embeddings and retrieval - bad context means bad answers, plus extra latency

core_ideas.idea: Efficient fine-tuning with LoRA, QLoRA and quantization makes custom LLMs accessible
core_ideas.why: You can adapt LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon etc. on consumer GPUs using 4-bit/8-bit training, LoRA adapters and SFTTrainer instead of full training
core_ideas.trade_off: Much lower cost, but you still need clean datasets, careful evaluation, and you risk overfitting if data is small or biased

core_ideas.idea: Agentic AI is about choosing the right design pattern - single agent vs multi-agent
core_ideas.why: For open-ended, multi-step tasks you need agents that can reason, use tools and work together; choice depends on task complexity, latency vs accuracy, cost and human oversight
core_ideas.trade_off: More agents and autonomy handle harder work but add complexity, cost, latency and harder debugging compared to simple deterministic code

core_ideas.idea: Production AI needs more than demos - open ecosystem, evaluation and deployment at scale
core_ideas.why: The open-source AI landscape moves fast; Google ADK and the State of Open Source AI guide show how to combine deterministic logic with LLM reasoning, manage context, evaluate and deploy reliably
core_ideas.trade_off: Open tools give flexibility and no vendor lock-in, but you must handle integration, maintenance, monitoring and scaling yourself

Shows the key choice: use RAG retrieval to add knowledge vs fine-tune the model itself

disagreements.point: Prompt-only hype vs deep building: video editing saves say 'RIP editing, just chat to edit' while fine-tuning saves say serious builders must go beyond prompting into LoRA, RAG and evaluation

RAG vs fine-tuning as the fix: Obelisk and agentic design saves present RAG as cheaper/better than retraining, while fine-tuning saves present LoRA/QLoRA as the way to customize models - pulling in opposite directions on when to retrieve vs when to train

gaps.why_it_matters: LoRA and vector embeddings only work as well as the data you feed them - bad data means biased or leaky models

gaps.missing: Cost, GPU sizing and latency optimization for production
